Alternative Grading Option: Take-Home Essays

The grading policies for this course are designed to be extremely flexible and accommodating. For nearly every student, the standard evaluation and engagement system absorbs absences, illness, and difficult weeks automatically, with no need for special arrangements. (See the Grading Policies page.)

Occasionally, a student needs accommodations beyond what that system can provide: for example, accommodations through Disability Resources and Services (DRS), or circumstances serious enough to affect the semester as a whole. In those cases, the course reverts to a classic format: take-home analytical essays.

Who This Applies To

This option is not something you can choose on your own, and it is not granted through individual requests to the instructor. It comes only through formal channels:

  • An accommodation letter from Disability Resources and Services (DRS), or
  • A request from your academic advisor or the Dean of Students office.

When a request comes through one of these channels, it will be granted.

If you have been placed in this option:

  • Your semester grade is based entirely on two essays. Your evaluation and engagement grades no longer count.
  • The switch is permanent. Once you move to this option, you cannot move back to the standard system.

How Your Grade Is Calculated

Assignment Weight
Midterm essay 40%
Final essay 60%

Deadlines

  • Midterm essay: due immediately after midterm break.

  • Final essay: due at the date and time of the course’s designated final exam. The essay is take-home: you do not need to go to the exam room. The exam slot simply sets the deadline.

  • No extensions. Late essays are not accepted.

  • Starting late: if this option is granted after the midterm essay deadline has passed, your final essay counts for 100% of your semester grade.

No AI. At All.

These essays work on the honor system. By submitting them, you agree that you have not used AI in any way, for either essay, other than tools explicitly designated in your DRS accommodation letter or another formal accommodation. That includes, but is not limited to:

  • Writing or drafting any part of the essay
  • Proofreading or editing
  • Literature review or research summaries
  • Summarizing your notes, the readings, or the lectures
  • Brainstorming, outlining, or generating arguments
  • Translation

“AI” means any generative AI tool, including chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot, AI writing assistants, and AI-generated summaries in search engines. If you are unsure whether something counts, assume that it does.

Fine print: ordinary spellcheck (the red squiggly underline) is fine. Yes, it is technically a form of AI too (see AI in This Course); this rule is about your prose, not your typos. Grammar and style tools that rewrite your sentences are not fine.

Each essay must begin with this signed statement:

I affirm that I did not use AI in any way in preparing or writing this essay, other than tools explicitly designated in my formal accommodations.
Signed: [your name]

Essays without the signed statement will not be accepted. Violations are handled under the University of Pittsburgh’s Academic Integrity Code.
